scenes.heading: Workflow Step Types
scenes.narration: Workflows. Workflow Step Types. In this video we review 7 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: Which step type should be used when a person must complete assigned work before the workflow can continue?
scenes.heading: A Participant step generates a work item for a user or group and waits for a person
scenes.body: Participant steps generate a work item, assign it to a user or group, and require a person to complete that item before the workflow advances.

scenes.question: Which step type runs automatically by the system and can be implemented in Java or ECMA script?
scenes.heading: A Process step runs automatically and is implemented by an ECMA script or a Java class
scenes.body: Section 4 says Process steps are executed automatically by the system and are implemented either by an ECMA script or a Java class.

scenes.question: What does a Container step do?
scenes.heading: A Container step starts another workflow model as a sub-workflow
scenes.body: The lesson says Container steps start another workflow model as a sub-workflow.

scenes.question: A scenario requires logic to choose which step should execute next. Which step type fits best?
scenes.heading: An OR Split and Join uses logic to decide which step to execute next
scenes.body: Section 4 says OR Split and Join use logic to decide which step to execute next.

scenes.question: Which step type allows multiple steps to run simultaneously?
scenes.heading: AND Split and Join allow multiple steps to run simultaneously
scenes.body: The speech states that AND Split and Join allow multiple steps to run simultaneously.

scenes.question: Which properties are shared by all workflow steps?
scenes.heading: All steps share Autoadvance and Timeout alerts, and the timeouts are scriptable
scenes.body: Section 4 says all steps share the common properties Autoadvance and Timeout alerts, and that timeouts are scriptable.

scenes.question: How does the Dynamic Participant step determine the assignee?
scenes.heading: It uses a service or script to choose the user at runtime instead of a fixed user
scenes.body: The Dynamic Participant step uses a service or script to choose the user who receives the work item at runtime instead of using a fixed user.
